newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UOB Malaysian unit in line for Tier-1.
newsitem.headline: UOB Malaysian unit in line for Tier-1.

text.p: Singapore's United Overseas Bank Ltd said on Friday its merged Malaysian subsidiaries, Chung Khiaw Bank (Malaysia) Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, is now ready for Tier-1 banking status.
The merged entity, effective from June 7 1997, will be called United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd or UOB(M), a bank statement said.
Under Malaysia's banking rules, Tier-1 status banks are allowed to operate in a more liberal regulatory environment.
Part of the requirements of a Tier-1 bank include having minimum shareholders' funds of 500 million ringgit which should increase to one billion by year 2000.
The statement said UOB(M) has assets of 11.1 billion ringgit and total shareholders' funds of 941 million ringgit as at December 31, 1996.
Group chairman Wee Cho Yaw said in the statement the merger was in line with the Malaysian government's efforts to rationalise the banking sector.
UOB(M) will have 25 branches in Malaysia after the merger.
It will be the 10th largest bank in Malaysia and the fourth largest among foreign-owned banks in the country in terms of total assets, said the statement.
